notes.ru: Modulatu difficillimum — супин на -u при прилагательном («труднейший для исполнения», как facile dictu). Meditatio здесь — «подготовка, упражнение», как в цицероновской паре meditatio atque exercitatio. Ср. у Феона: энгармонический род «труднее всего для пения» (δυσμελῳδητότατον), «требует большой привычки» и потому нелегко входит в употребление.
notes.en: Modulatu difficillimum: supine in -u with an adjective (“most difficult to perform”, like facile dictu). Meditatio here is “preparation, practice”, as in Cicero's pair meditatio atque exercitatio. Cf. Theon: the enharmonic genus is “the hardest to sing” (δυσμελῳδητότατον), “needs much habituation”, and so does not easily come into use.
notes.source: Lewis & Short s.v. meditatio (Cic. Div. 2.96) and s.v. modulatus, -us [checked]; Allen and Greenough § 510 (supine in -u with adjectives) [checked]; Theon, ed. Hiller p. 56.1–3 [checked]

segments.ru: Диатонический же — простой, благородный и более естественный; поэтому его допускает и Платон.
segments.en: The diatonic, on the other hand, is simple and noble and more natural; that is why Plato too admits it.

notes.ru: Simplum — от simplus (а не simplex), «простой». То же суждение — у Феона: диатонический род «простой, благородный и более согласный с природой; потому Платон скорее принимает его». Феон имеет в виду диатоническое деление в «Тимее» (35b–36b); в «Государстве» Платон рассуждает о ладах, а не о родах.
notes.en: Simplum is from simplus (not simplex), “simple”. The same judgement is in Theon: the diatonic genus is “simple, noble and more in accordance with nature; hence Plato rather adopts it”. Theon has in mind the diatonic division in the Timaeus (35b–36b); in the Republic Plato discusses modes, not genera.
notes.source: Lewis & Short s.v. simplus [checked]; Theon, ed. Hiller p. 56.3–5 and p. 63.25 (ὁ δὲ Πλάτων καὶ γένος διάτονον …; Hiller's apparatus: Tim. p. 35 sq.) [checked]; Plato, Republic 398e–399c [from memory]

segments.ru: Каждый же из них, в свою очередь, видоизменяется и распределяется на многие подразделения, различия и роды мелодий: лад называется то лидийским, то фригийским, то дорийским; и от любого из них происходят пеан, гименей, эксодий и все, сколько их ни есть, роды мелодий.
segments.en: Each of these, in turn, is varied and distributed into many divisions and differences and genera of melody: the mode is called now Lydian, now Phrygian, now Dorian; and from any one of them arise the paean, the hymenaeus, the exodius, and all the genera of melody there are.

notes.ru: Modulus (букв. «мера, размер») здесь — «лад»; ср. modulatio «мелодия», modulatu «для исполнения» (V62). Genera modulationum — «роды мелодий» в общем смысле «виды», а не три рода тетрахорда; genus всюду передаётся «род» / “genus”, как и в версии Ксиландра (X56–X57). Paeeon (в печати Pæéon) — пеан, песнь в честь Аполлона; Hymenaeus — свадебная песнь; Exodius (мужской род, в согласии с Paeeon и Hymenaeus; словарная форма — exodium) — заключительная песнь (exodium — пьеса, исполнявшаяся в конце представления). Ксиландр пишет Paean, Hymenaeus, Exodius и cantilena вместо modulus.
notes.en: Modulus (literally “measure”) here means “mode”; cf. modulatio “melody”, modulatu “to perform” (V62). Genera modulationum are genera of melody in the general sense of “kinds”, not the three genera of the tetrachord; genus is rendered «род» / “genus” throughout, as in Xylander’s version (X56–X57). Paeeon (printed Pæéon) is the paean, the song to Apollo; Hymenaeus the wedding song; Exodius (masculine, in agreement with Paeeon and Hymenaeus; the dictionary word is exodium) the closing song (the exodium was a piece performed at the end of a show). Xylander has Paean, Hymenaeus, Exodius, and cantilena instead of modulus.
notes.source: Lewis & Short s.v. modulus, s.v. exodium [checked]; Gaffiot 2016 s.v. modulus ¶ 4 (“mesure [en t. de musique], mode, mélodie”) [checked]; Xylander X56 in latin-texts.json [checked]

segments.ru: Ведь не одним только изменением интервалов и не одним только их различием, но и более медленными и стремительными переходами, а также паузами и течениями, и различными касаниями и ударами, сообразно различной мере [движений] руки, создаются бесчисленные и разнообразные мелодии.
segments.en: For not by the change of intervals alone, nor by their difference alone, but also by slower and quicker transitions, by pauses too and flowings, and by various touches and strokes, according to the varied measure of the hand, are infinite and diverse melodies produced.

notes.ru: Pausa — «остановка, пауза» (в средневековой теории — пауза в пении); fluxus — «течение», непрерывное движение, противоположное паузе. Tactus и pulsus — «касание» и «удар» (по струне). Temperamentum — «соразмерность, должная мера»: исполнение зависит от того, как соразмеряет свои движения рука.
notes.en: Pausa is “stop, pause” (in medieval theory a rest in singing); fluxus “flowing”, continuous movement as opposed to the pause. Tactus and pulsus are “touch” and “stroke” (of the string). Temperamentum is “due measure, proportion”: performance depends on how the hand measures its movements.
notes.source: Lewis & Short s.v. pausa, fluxus, tactus, pulsus, temperamentum [checked]; DMLBS s.v. pausa 1b (mus.) [checked]

doubts.issue: temperamentum can be “mixture in due proportion”, “measure, moderation” or “regulation”; the bracketed addition is needed in Russian.
doubts.options: «сообразно различной мере [движений] руки» / “according to the varied measure of the hand”; «смотря по различному владению рукой» / “according to the varied management of the hand”.
doubts.choice: “measure”, the dictionary sense closest to the word, without paraphrase in English; Russian needs [движений].
doubts.evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. temperamentum [checked]
doubts.alternative_ru: смотря по различному владению рукой
doubts.alternative_en: according to the varied management of the hand

segments.ru: Конец «Музыки».
segments.en: End of the Music.

the whole of things
terms.evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. universitas (in universitate rerum, Cic. N. D. 1.120) [checked]

terms.ru: кварта (у Ксиландра в X28–X30 и X35, где греческое название противопоставлено латинскому quarta: диатессарон)

the octave, 2:1; Xylander explains the name as per omnes, hoc est, per octo (X29), Vinet as per octo (V34–V35)

terms.en: the double octave (in Xylander X30: disdiapason)

terms.meaning_here: 8:3 and 3:1; Vinet calls them, with the double octave, posteriora intervalla “the subsequent intervals” (V35)

modern name of the double octave (X42)

summary: Both Latin versions were translated in full, each into Russian and English directly from the reading text: Xylander in 58 segments, Vinet in 66; a translator and a reviser worked on each version separately, and the assembler compared every segment with the Latin once more and checked the terminology of each version against itself and against about.md. The hardest passage is the division of the tone with the excursus on the unit and the square (X18–X25, V22–V30): Xylander makes the semitone 'as it were half' and the diesis 'as it were a quarter' of 9:8 and divides it geometrically (√(9/8)), whereas Vinet gives 'eight and a half' and 'eight and a quarter' against eight (17:16, 33:32), with a figure on p. 44, before he too appeals to a geometrical division. Xylander's Latin is hard to construe in several places (X23 Numerorum, X24 quod propositum dupli esse constat, X38 qua … habet, X26 compositae beside 'incomposita autem dicuntur'); the reading text is translated in each case and the alternatives are argued in text_issues. The versions differ most in terminology and in their handling of the Greek: Xylander glosses paraphonon/antiphonon with his own calques assonans/obsonans and sets the Greek interval names against the Latin names of his day (quarta, quinta, octava, decima quinta), so those names are transliterated in X28–X30 and X35; Vinet leaves paraphonum/antiphonum unglossed, calls the incomposite intervals simplicia, explains Dia-pason only as 'through eight', and builds the chain convenientia–conveniens–convenire where Xylander has harmoniae particeps and consonantia. They also differ in substance in X57/V65 (obliquioribus 'more oblique' against lentioribus 'slower'), in V05, where Vinet identifies music with the universe itself, and in the 'sixteen-string' scheme, which Xylander glosses as an instrument of sixteen strings (X15), while Vinet keeps the Greek word, rendered here as a system (V18, V49). Both versions transmit the statement that the fourth is two tones, a semitone and a nameless remainder smaller than a diesis, and that the octave is exactly six tones (X34, V39); this contradicts the ratios they give and is translated as it stands, with the arithmetic in the checks. Every ratio and count in the checks was recomputed and is correct, and a script confirmed that every ratio name in the running text carries its bracket, except semisesquioctave (about.md §4.3) and Xylander's parenthetic 'superbipartient by thirds', which glosses the 8:3 already bracketed. In assembling, the following inconsistencies were fixed: in Xylander's English 'the octave with the fourth/fifth' became 'the octave and a fourth/fifth' (X30, X31, X34, X35 and the X31 note), as about.md §4.2 requires; in Vinet's English V64 'kinds of melody' became 'genera of melody', so that genus is 'genus' throughout both versions, and 'exodium' became 'exodius', the form both translators print; Xylander's 'relaxation of the breath' (X41) became 'slackening', the rendering of the same pair in Vinet (V47); in X04 the English for nimirum became 'indeed', in agreement with the Russian and with X06; in X45 the Russian for conficitur became «составляется», as elsewhere in the version; and the X28 note now states exactly where the Greek interval names are transliterated. The terms were merged into 124 entries, 45 of them common to both versions; where the versions render the same Latin word differently (modulatio, paraphonum/antiphonum, the fifteen- and sixteen-string words, the note names), the entries say why. Least sure are the renderings of Xylander's coinages and rare words (assonans/obsonans as «призвучное»/«противозвучное» and 'sounding-to'/'sounding-against'; modulatio as 'modulation' in X44; mansio, fluxus, obliquioribus), 'mese monos' and 'Mese solum', the Russian «диапазон» for the transliterated diapason, and the bracketed [instrument]/[system] of V18. A reviewer should check first X24 (construction), X26 (compositae), X32 and V37 (unequal time read as succession), X34 and V39 (the remainder), V22 with its figure, and V18. Contamination: a footnote in von Jan's edition that quotes the Greek text was met by the Xylander translator and not used; the same page was opened during the work on Vinet's version, where no forbidden material was reported; both are recorded.
